schema.quotationText: Knowledge comes, but wisdom lingers, and I linger on the shore,
schema.webPageName: Who really said 'Knowledge comes, but wisdom lingers'?
schema.verdictNote: Alfred Lord Tennyson wrote the line in Locksley Hall (1842). Coolidge quoted the poet; he did not originate the words.
schema.claimReviewed: Calvin Coolidge originated the words “Knowledge comes, but wisdom lingers.”
schema.faqAnswer: Tennyson wrote these words in Locksley Hall (1842), line 141. Coolidge later quoted the poet; Coolidge is not their originator.

sourcesVerified.claim: The fetched Locksley Hall transcription supplies line 141. Coolidge’s Wikiquote entry explicitly says he was quoting Tennyson. The poem’s publication date of 1842 is corroborated by its reference article.
The entry identifies Coolidge as quoting Tennyson.
